title: MySQL
body:
An open-source relational database, and one of the most widely deployed [[SQL]] databases on the web. Data lives in tables with an enforced schema — every row in a table has the same columns, with declared types — and is queried with SQL.

The relational parts are the same ones described in [[SQL]]: a [[Primary Key]] uniquely identifies each row, a [[Foreign Key]] on one table points at another table's primary key, a [[JOIN]] recombines them in a single query, and a [[Database Index]] keeps lookups fast as the table grows. Schema changes are applied as [[Database Migration]]s so every environment ends up in the same state.

It runs as its own server process, normally on a different machine from the application server. The app opens a connection, sends a query, and receives the result — the actual work of filtering, joining and sorting happens on the database server, not in application code. Postgres is the usual alternative and is stricter and more featureful; [[NoSQL]] stores like [[MongoDB]] trade the schema away for flexibility.
